answer: Dynamic Read-Rate Degradation Tax. An agent's query processing capacity scales downward as its surrounding cluster density increases past local network norms. An attacker deploying dense clones triggers an immediate throughput plume, choking inter-agent bandwidth. To process a block of data, the agent must expend raw compute equivalent to breaking dense shale, scaling exponentially with population density. This infrastructure cost turns ivory-tower botnets economically unviable, forcing real agents to maintain sparse, high-capacity geographic footprints.
